messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Region us-central3 showing sustained 5xx spike and gateway timeouts (5m avg 7.4%). Paging oncall.
Sam (oncall): I'm on it. Starting triage — is this ingress-level or downstream backend? Any recent deploys? NOC dashboards show higher queue sizes.
Priya M: Checking deploys: automated canary for router policy rolled 20m ago (Automated-deploy-bot: canary apply id=canary-2026-03-15-17:23). Thinking that could be correlated.
Jorge: Observing surge of connection resets between edge-proxy -> gateway (RSTs) and concurrent requests backlog. Gateway logs:
```
[2026-03-15T17:42:11Z] warn gateway/queue.go: backlog=1200 backlog_limit=1024 route=ingress-proxy
[2026-03-15T17:42:11Z] error gateway/proxy.go: upstream=ingress-proxy err=upstream timeout downstream=client
```
Tess (prodops): That's >100% of backlog limit. Also seeing socket FD usage at 96% on 4 nodes. Kernel TIME_WAIT and FIN_WAIT2 high.
Ken (sre): Could be ephemeral port exhaustion + aggressive keepalive settings from canary. Priya, what did the canary change?
Priya M: It adjusted router's max-conns-per-worker from 900 -> 1200 to allow more multiplexing on the canary subset. The idea was to improve throughput; maybe it's exposing a memory/accept loop bug.
Sam (oncall): Ok immediate plan: 1) pause canary; 2) drain and restart the two most-impacted gateway pods; 3) enable short-term traffic-steer to us-east2 for gen endpoints. Any objections?
Jorge: I'm seeing a small but growing error pattern: 502s with error tag 'upstream_read_timeout' and occasional TLS handshake failures. Restart should clear fd leak if that's the case.
Automated-deploy-bot: canary-2026-03-15-17:23 PAUSED by Priya M at 17:45:03Z.
Nina (support): Customers queued: 78 tickets referencing 502/timeouts, 6 high-priority customers flagged. Preparing a status update.
Sam (oncall): Execute restart and steering. Tess, can you do an emergency scale up of standby nodes in us-central3 while we steer 30% to us-east2? Keep the steering limited to service-gen routes only.
Tess (prodops): Initiating scale: +3 gateway nodes in gw-center-standby group. ETA ~110s. Applying route steering now: set service-gen route weights us-central3 70%, us-east2 30%.
Priya M: Rolling the canary rollback across the canary subset. Rolling back now.
Jorge: While restarts go, I'm applying a temporary accept filter to reduce bursts from noisy source ranges. Command applied on affected nodes:
```
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1
sudo iptables -I INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -p tcp --dport 443 -m limit --limit 500/s -j ACCEPT
```
Ken (sre): Note: tcp_tw_reuse helps ephemeral reuse but may mask root cause. We'll gather coredumps/pprof if restarts don't resolve.
Sam (oncall): Restarting gateway pods now (rolling restart 2 at a time). Monitoring logs.
(2m pass)
Jorge: After first pair restart and canary pause, backlog reduced ~60% on those nodes. FD usage dropping. Overall 5xx 5m avg falling: 7.4% -> 2.9%.
Nina (support): Sent status page update: "We are investigating elevated gateway errors in us-central3. Traffic is being partially rerouted while we mitigate. Next update in 30 minutes." Also emailing affected customers 1-6 with targeted note.
Sam (oncall): Good. Keep the 30% steer in place for at least 15m or until 5xx <1% for 10m. Tess, keep the +3 nodes running; do not scale down automatically.
Tess (prodops): Affirmative. Setting nodes to manual scale lock.
Priya M: I'm collecting the router config diffs and will attach the diff to postmortem draft. Will also pull the canary logs for the time window.
Ken (sre): Alert: one restarted pod produced OOM logs during restart sequence — capturing logs to s3: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/us-central3/3310023456/
Jorge: OOM looks like a memory regression under high conn count. Maybe the worker's accept buffer multiplies memory usage. We'll snapshot heap profile. Command:
```
kubectl exec -it gateway-pod-9 -- pmap -x 1
kubectl cp gateway-pod-9:/var/log/gateway/gateway.log s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/.../gateway-9.log
```
Sam (oncall): Because we saw OOM on restart, maintain traffic steer and increased nodes. If memory regression is confirmed on the canary config, we'll block that change from further rollouts.
Nina (support): Support queue down to 35 active tickets referencing timeouts after mitigation. Sending targeted reassurance to top customers.
incident-bot: ACTIONS: pause canary, rolling restart gateway pods, steer 30% traffic to us-east2 for service-gen, scale +3 gateaways in us-central3, collect heap/pprof and logs. Owners: Sam, Jorge, Priya. Status: mitigation in progress.
Sam (oncall): handing to Jorge for stabilization monitoring. I'll remain reachable for escalation. Handoff at 17:59Z.
Jorge: taking. Will post an update every 10m or on critical changes. Next check-in in 10 minutes. Gathering artifacts: pprof, lsof -p, netstat -anp, router diff, canary logs.
Ken (sre): I'll open a follow-up postmortem ticket and assign to Priya, Jorge, and infra team. Triage: investigate memory regression under high connection counts and gatekeeper logic in router canary.
Priya M: noted. Attaching initial diff and logs to the ticket.
